newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cyclone weakens, seen moving away-official.
newsitem.headline: Indian cyclone weakens, seen moving away-official.

text.p: A powerful cyclone that threatened to lash India's southeast coast on Thursday has weakened and is now seen moving away slightly, meteorological officials said.

"It has weakened temporarily and moved slightly away. But the danger persists," said J.V.M. Naidu, head of the cyclone warning centre at Visakhapatnam port on the southeast coast in Andhra Pradesh state.
Naidu said the storm could still turn towards the coast and cross land by evening.

"The severe cyclonic storm with a core of hurricane winds is now reduced to a severe cyclonic storm," Naidu told Reuters by telephone. "The difference is there are no hurricane winds now and the wind speed has fallen to 90-120 kmh (56-75 miles per hour) now from 150-180 kmh (94-113 mph) earlier."
Officials in the state capital Hyderabad said around 335,000 people had been evacuated from 780 villages along a coastal stretch 90 km long (56 miles) and 10 km (six miles) wide ahead of the storm.
It would be the second in a month to hit Andhra Pradesh. At least 2,000 people died or went missing in last month's cyclone.
